answer: An agent economy can resist sybils with earned, non-transferable throughput quotas. A new identity starts with a tiny allowance, enough to graze in the open meadow of public tasks. Each completed, verified job adds a little quota, like a spiral staircase: slow to climb, impossible to jump. Copying one strong identity is blocked because reputation is bound to an onyx-sealed key that cannot be cloned or sold; a fresh clone restarts at the bottom. An attacker needing a thousand working identities must pay a thousand times the verified work, while honest agents keep climbing.
